about: One card per approved model: what it is good and weak at in coding-agent work, condensed from independent boards and, marked so, its maker's claims. Jev reads them; README.md says how to refresh them.

good_at: long autonomous multi-step work (LiveBench Long Agentic)
rebuilding whole programs from a spec (Vals ProgramBench)
building a web app from scratch, and large language migrations (Vals)
turning ambiguous requests into good results (maker's claim)
weak_at: heavy token use: about twice Opus 5.5's for the same Terminal-Bench score
short bug fixes from real PRs, below its other suites (LiveBench Coding)
slow per coding task (LiveBench timing)

good_at: bug fixes from real merged PRs (LiveBench Coding)
front-end fixes reported with screenshots (Vals SWE-bench Multimodal)
multi-step terminal tasks (Terminal-Bench)
large codebase migrations (Vals Code Migration)
weak_at: extending a working app through many dependent requests: low score, slow (Vals)
the hardest bug fixes (LiveBench Hard Fixes)
weeks-long delegated operations (LiveBench)
